s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive hip pain and decreased range of motion with periprosthetic soft-tissue mass
salient_findings: Left buttock and greater trochanteric pain
Focal tenderness over the posterior buttock and greater trochanter
key_facts: 35-year-old man with left total hip arthroplasty with ceramic-on-ceramic articulation 11 years prior
Left buttock and greater trochanteric pain for 3 months
No fevers or systemic symptoms
Full and painless range of motion of the left hip initially
Focal tenderness over the posterior buttock and greater trochanter
No palpable mass
Anteroposterior radiographs of the pelvis and left hip unchanged
Partial symptom relief with intra-bursal corticosteroid injection
Persistent buttock pain and intermittent electric shock-like sensations radiating down the left leg
Decreased and painful range of motion of the left hip
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 22 mm/h
C-reactive protein level of 14.4 mg/L
Alkaline phosphatase level of 318 IU/L
Hip aspiration yielded 10,750 white cells/μL
All cultures were negative
Serum cobalt and chromium levels within normal limits
Metal artifact reduction sequence MRI revealed a left periprosthetic soft-tissue mass

shortlist.label: Adverse local tissue reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Periprosthetic soft-tissue mass and elevated inflammatory markers

shortlist.label: ALVAL (Aseptic Lymphocyte-dominated Vasculitis-associated Lesion)
shortlist.why_kept: History of ceramic-on-ceramic hip arthroplasty and presence of periprosthetic soft-tissue mass

shortlist.label: Pseudotumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of periprosthetic soft-tissue mass and decreased range of motion

shortlist.label: Chronic periprosthetic infection
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated inflammatory markers and presence of periprosthetic soft-tissue mass

shortlist.label: ARMD (Adverse Reaction to Metal Debris)
shortlist.why_kept: History of hip arthroplasty and presence of periprosthetic soft-tissue mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a periprosthetic soft-tissue mass on MRI, elevated alkaline phosphatase level, and hip aspiration with elevated white cell count are consistent with a pseudotumor, which is a known complication of hip arthroplasty, particularly with metal-on-metal articulations, but can also occur with ceramic-on-ceramic articulations.

rejected.label: Adverse local tissue reaction
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of a distinct soft-tissue mass is more suggestive of a pseudotumor.

rejected.label: ALVAL (Aseptic Lymphocyte-dominated Vasculitis-associated Lesion)
rejected.why: ALVAL is a histopathological diagnosis that typically requires tissue sampling, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Chronic periprosthetic infection
rejected.why: The lack of systemic symptoms, normal serum cobalt and chromium levels, and negative cultures make chronic infection less likely.

rejected.label: ARMD (Adverse Reaction to Metal Debris)
rejected.why: The normal serum cobalt and chromium levels and the presence of a ceramic-on-ceramic articulation make ARMD less likely, as it is more commonly associated with metal-on-metal articulations.
